label: copy-phase input w, strongest when the next output is t or late in long sequences
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, and almost only when the fed-back input is w (98% of activation mass; the rest is small activations on input t right after a w or t). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Copy-phase w is necessary but nowhere near sufficient: only about 5% of copy-phase w steps fire. Activation is much stronger and more reliable when the token being output right after w is t (the original bigram w t; precision 0.51, rising to 0.79 when recall_idx >= 3, and this case holds about half of all mass). The top examples are all w followed by output t. The rate also rises with step position and L (lift 10-13x at t = 16-17, about 0 before t = 8), so late copy-phase w in L = 9 sequences fires weakly even without a following t. The disjunction gets dev F1 0.42 and mass recall 0.73; plain copy-phase w gets recall 0.96 but precision 0.05. It does not fire on w in the original phase, or on other letters except weak t.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: w, t, -, o, m, p; least: <DEL>, x, r, u) and the token being output (most: t, w, e, 2, c, u; least: h, n, -, f); timing cues that raise it most: t=17, recall_idx=8, L=9 & t=17.
